name: CIRCA demo content
notes: Demo identities (names, bios and captions are invented) on licensed stock footage of real performers from Mixkit, with licensed music from Mixkit's composers. The performers are not the people named. Real NASA shows and episodes; long ones are excerpted. NASA media is public domain; NASA does not endorse CIRCA. Sample listeners and every listening figure are simulated.

creators.name: Ellis Rae
creators.bio: Writes in a brick-walled room in Bushwick with one good microphone and the lights low. Low Light is the first thing he's let leave the room.

creators.name: Marisol Vega
creators.bio: Grew up on her grandmother's bolero records and plays them back through a soul band. Candela was recorded live in one afternoon.

creators.name: Juniper & Lowe
creators.bio: A guitar and a banjo that met busking outside the same coffee shop. They still play the street on Sundays.

creators.name: Kairo Banks
creators.bio: Records at night after shifts at his uncle's shop. Night Shift is the sound of that commute.

creators.name: Nova Lin
creators.bio: Plays every small club that will have her and treats each like an arena. Afterglow is written for the walk home after.

creators.name: The Halyards
creators.bio: Four friends from a sailing town who got loud. Undertow is their first single on a real label.

creators.name: Houston We Have a Podcast
creators.bio: NASA Johnson Space Center's official podcast: long-form conversations with the people who fly, train and plan human spaceflight.

creators.name: Rocket Ranch
creators.bio: NASA Kennedy Space Center's podcast about the people and work behind getting to space.

creators.name: Down to Earth: Conversations
creators.bio: A NASA series pairing astronauts with students to talk about what living and working in space is really like.

creators.name: NASA Science Live
creators.bio: A live show where NASA scientists answer questions about the universe, from black holes to rising seas.

creators.name: Dex Holloway
creators.bio: Plays the late set at a restaurant that closed its kitchen years ago. Blue Booth is named after his table.

creators.name: Inés Moreau
creators.bio: Trained in conservatory, now writes for rooftops and film. Plays her grandfather's violin.

creators.name: The Arden Strings
creators.bio: Two violinists who met in a pit orchestra and kept playing after the curtain. Glasswork is their first record.

creators.name: SOLA
creators.bio: Plays long sets and short sleeves. Pink Hour is the track that closes every night.

creators.name: Salón Azul Quartet
creators.bio: A house band for an old ballroom that never stopped having parties. Late Seating is their dinner-set closer.

creators.name: Canal Street Brass
creators.bio: Horns that play wherever the echo is best: underpasses, stairwells, the odd wedding.

creators.name: Lucía Paz
creators.bio: Writes outside, mostly. Sol de Tarde was finished on a fallen tree by the river.

creators.name: Aurelio Fen
creators.bio: A pianist who scores silent films for fun. Nocturne is for the walk home in October.

creators.name: Space to Ground
creators.bio: NASA's weekly update on what's happening aboard the International Space Station.

creators.name: What’s Up
creators.bio: NASA JPL's monthly guide to what to look for in the night sky.

creators.name: NASA ScienceCasts
creators.bio: Short NASA episodes on the science behind what's in the news and in the sky.

creators.name: Gravity Assist
creators.bio: NASA's podcast of conversations with scientists about the search for life and the worlds of our solar system.

creators.name: NASA in Silicon Valley Live
creators.bio: A talk show from NASA's Ames Research Center with the scientists, researchers and engineers pushing innovation.

creators.name: NASA Explorers
creators.bio: A NASA documentary series following researchers through an experiment, from the lab to the space station.

episodes.title: Mental Health with Shinedown
episodes.topic: In honour of Mental Health Awareness Month, the rock band Shinedown talks with an astronaut and NASA researchers about mental health for touring band members, orbiting astronauts and everyone.

episodes.title: Artemis Flight Directors
episodes.topic: Gary Jordan walks through Artemis I, the uncrewed test flight around the Moon, with lead flight director Rick LaBrode and ascent and entry flight director Judd Frieling.

episodes.title: Landing on Mars, Protecting Mars
episodes.topic: Dr. Moogega Cooper, planetary protection lead for the Perseverance rover at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, on the manoeuvres needed to land on Mars and how her team protects it.

episodes.title: Sensory Overload
episodes.topic: Astronaut Sunita Williams and environmental studies student Adrien Prouty explore what it's like to do a spacewalk on the International Space Station.

episodes.title: The Miracle Planet
episodes.topic: Suni and Adrien discuss protecting our planet's environment, and share their closing thoughts.

episodes.title: Black Hole 101
episodes.topic: NASA scientists on what black holes are, and how we know they exist even though we can't see them.

episodes.title: Space Gardening
episodes.topic: NASA's weekly update from the International Space Station: this week, growing plants in orbit.

episodes.title: April 2026 Skywatching
episodes.topic: Mercury at its brightest for the year, the Lyrid meteor shower and a bright new comet in April's night sky.

highlight.title: What to look for this month

episodes.title: Eye on Neptune
episodes.topic: Neptune reaches opposition, giving sky watchers and astronomers a chance to observe a planet invisible to the naked eye.

highlight.title: Watching a planet you can't see

episodes.title: Looking for Life in Ancient Lakes
episodes.topic: Astrobiologist Kennda Lynch on studying ancient lakes on Earth that resemble the Perseverance rover's landing site on Mars, to help search for life.

highlight.title: Mars, by way of Earth's lakes

episodes.title: Is There Life on Mars?
episodes.topic: How NASA is developing new tools to search for life on Mars.

highlight.title: New tools for an old question

episodes.title: On Station
episodes.topic: The researchers' experiment reaches the International Space Station: astronauts test the samples in microgravity while the team on Earth runs its own part.

ic-ellis-session.text: Leaving the crack in is the whole point. Please never fix it.
Already know this one is going to wreck me.
That breath before the chorus. Twice.

ic-ellis-rehearsal.text: Danny on guitar is the secret weapon.
The chord change at 0:07 is a whole other song.

ic-halyards-soundcheck.text: That window light should get a writing credit.
Would happily listen to forty minutes of this soundcheck.
Mira says thank you. The light says nothing.

ic-halyards-crowd.text: I was in that crowd. Still can’t hear properly.
Undertow live is a different animal.

ic-nova-dance.text: See you in that room tonight, front left.
The choreo is going to be everywhere by summer.
front left gets the encore wave.

ic-juniper-lowe-street.text: The kid dancing deserves a writing credit.
splitting it 50/50 with the kid, yes.

ic-kairo-booth.text: Verse two. Put it out exactly like this.
Played this on my commute three times today.

ic-marisol-warmup.text: the room does half the work, honestly.

ic-nova-stage.text: I could hear it from the bar. Loudest crowd of the year.

ic-dex-packing-up.text: Same chair every night is the most jazz sentence ever written.

ic-ines-close.text: Scales never sounded this good at 7am.

ic-ines-case.text: he would ask why it took me so long.

ic-sola-setup.text: The venue power held. Barely. Best night of the year.

ic-sola-decks.text: you were the loud ones at the front, weren’t you.

ic-salon-drums.text: Rubén is a menace in the best way.

ic-arden-take.text: Take four is the one. Trust me.

ic-lucia-log.text: the log gets a writing credit.

ic-canal-room.text: That room has the best echo in the city.
